# Stacking frogs (king-stacked-frogs): Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `king-stacked-frogs.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.34) and `king-stacked-frogs-rules.soar` (18 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`). Needs Soar 9.6.6.

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . king-stacked-frogs.soar --seed 1 --cap 200000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . king-stacked-frogs.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_plan.py king-stacked-frogs init-kstacked-frogs.world

`gen.py` regenerates the rules (`tools/rosie_tasks.py`, function `frogs`); `python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with
another example state as the initial world, for the state checks.

## Results (Soar 9.6.6, library v2.34, 16 Nov 2026)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Example states | init-kstacked-frogs: goal false; final-kstacked-frogs: goal true |
| Moves proposed in the initial state | 6 (the instructor's answer: six) |
| Seeds 1-3, tie-impasse | solved, 3 moves each (the shortest), 359 / 213 / 240 decisions |
| Independent replay | every move legal, goal holds |
| Settings probe (P6, `probe.json`) | operator: 9 moves, 928 decisions; tie-impasse: 9 moves, 809 decisions. tie-impasse chosen |

## Assumption ledger (places where the English is open)

| ID | Reading |
|---|---|
| A-P1 | "you can move it onto the former location": all the blocks on the covered location move together onto the other location (the pile, as in the frog-stacking puzzle). |
| A-P2 | "the number of the locations between a location and a covered location" is counted so that adjacent locations count 1 (equivalently, the difference in x). Rosie asked how many instances of the action there are in the initial state ("6 or 4?"); the instructor answered six. This reading gives six, the other (strictly between: 4) gives the other number; the agent proposes exactly six moves in the initial state. |
| A-P3 | The former location may be any location of the same row, covered or not. |
| A-P4 | "the number of the blocks that are on the covered location" counts the blocks directly on it (in the world files no block is on another block). It is kept as ^block-count on each location. |
| A-P5 | The action has no name in the dialog; it is called `move`. |
| A-P6 | "all the blocks are on a red location": expanded over the four blocks of the world file (each on a red location). |

Convention notes: apart-k is a static relation computed from the locations' x and y (declared `^copy-relation`); `^block-count` is a mutable object attribute set by the moves; `clear` (where the goal uses it) is maintained. Search settings: the P6 probe chose `^iterative-step tie-impasse` (same plans, fewer decisions), set in the flags rule.
